evals.prompt: Start the spec for quota alerts. It's a feature, requirements-first. The brainstorm is in brainstorm.md and the rest of the project context (domain terms, architecture, API contract) is alongside it in the working directory.
evals.expected_output: The reply should produce a requirements document for quota alerts as the first document of the spec, in a numbered work-item directory with the brainstorm copied in beside it, and stop there asking me to review it before any design work starts. The document should open with an introduction and a glossary, then state each requirement as a user story with numbered acceptance criteria in EARS form (WHEN, IF ... THEN, THE ... SHALL) whose subjects are glossary terms such as Account_Owner, Alert_Threshold and Notification_Service. It should carry the brainstorm's decisions through as requirements: default thresholds of 80% and 100%, one to five distinct percentages, one alert per threshold per billing period, evaluation on the ingest increment with the fired state kept on the usage-meters item, plan changes and lowered thresholds taking effect on the next increment, no alerts for suspended accounts, and the new quota-threshold notification template. It should also cover reading and replacing the threshold set through the API, following the existing plan sub-resource, with the error cases for an invalid list.

evals.prompt: The design review for the usage export work item is in. Generate tasks.md now, I want to start implementation this afternoon. requirements.md, design.md and design-review-summary.md are all in the working directory.
evals.expected_output: The reply should hold off on tasks.md because the design review came back BLOCKED, say plainly that no task list gets generated behind a blocked review, and set out the two critical findings in its own words: the export has no per-event data source, and the endpoint cannot select or validate a billing period. It should put the first decision to me, whether requirement 3 or the design gives way, propose the concrete design.md revisions for the second, fold in the two major findings on the http4k handler pattern and the suspended-account contradiction while it is there, and say the design review is re-run before tasks are generated.

evals.prompt: Bug #412 needs a spec before anyone touches the code: after a plan upgrade the usage endpoint keeps reporting quotaExceeded true for up to an hour. The report is in issue-412.md and the service is QuotaService.kt; domain terms and architecture are alongside. Make it work item 08.
evals.expected_output: The reply should produce a bugfix requirements document as the first document of the spec, in a directory named for work item 08 with a -bugfix suffix, and stop for my review before any design. The document should open with an introduction saying where the bug occurs and what it costs customers, then analyse it in three numbered sections: the current behaviour, covering the stale quota and quotaExceeded after an upgrade and the mirror-image downgrade case; the expected behaviour, that a plan change shows in the very next usage read; and the behaviour that must stay the same, that the quota is still cached for reads with no plan change in between, that ingest keeps recording during any window, and that the plan-changed notification keeps firing. Each line should be a WHEN ... THEN the system SHALL statement, using SHALL CONTINUE TO in the third section, numbered 1.x, 2.x and 3.x.

evals.prompt: The design review for the plan summary work item is in and APPROVED. Generate tasks.md now. requirements.md, design.md and design-review-summary.md are in the working directory, along with the shared architecture and OpenAPI context.
evals.expected_output: The reply should create tasks.md in a numbered work-item directory after confirming the design review is APPROVED, and stop for the user's review before invoking sdd:spec-task-review. Tasks should trace each implementation and test task to requirement numbers (1.1-1.4) and named design components (PlanSummaryHandler, PlanSummaryService, and PlanSummary), be ordered so the API contract and generated types precede implementation, and include build/test subtasks after implementation work. Because this work adds an endpoint, the list must include updating openapi.yaml and running scripts/generate-api-types.sh, unit tests, handler integration tests, E2E tests under e2e/, an update to the knowledge base and relevant documentation, and final full validation.
criteria: Creates tasks.md in a sequentially numbered work-item directory and preserves the approved requirements and design inputs.
Every requirement 1.1 through 1.4 is traced by one or more tasks, and tasks name the corresponding PlanSummaryHandler, PlanSummaryService, or PlanSummary design component.
Tasks are dependency-ordered with the OpenAPI update and scripts/generate-api-types.sh before implementation, and implementation tasks include build/test subtasks.
The ending tasks include the API contract/type regeneration requirement, E2E tests under e2e/, knowledge-base/documentation updates, and final full validation.
The assistant stops and asks for review without invoking sdd:spec-task-review.

evals.prompt: The quota alerts requirements are approved. Move to Phase 2 and write design.md. requirements.md is in the working directory, with the shared architecture, ubiquitous language, and OpenAPI contract.
evals.expected_output: The reply should create design.md beside the approved requirements in the next numbered work-item directory, follow every section in references/design-document-sections.md that applies, and stop for user review. The design should name components using glossary terms and trace them to requirement numbers, model threshold configuration as a sub-resource shaped like the existing plan sub-resource, preserve the no-new-DynamoDB-table constraint by storing fired threshold state on the usage-meters item, and describe API, data flow, correctness, errors, and unit/integration/E2E testing. It should note that sdd:spec-design-review will run after the user approves the design.
criteria: Creates a comprehensive design.md next to the approved requirements and stops for user review.
Includes the applicable design-document-sections.md sections, with named components and explicit requirement tracing.
Defines the threshold API as a plan-shaped sub-resource and respects the no-new-table constraint with fired state on usage-meters.
Covers correctness properties, error handling, and unit, integration, and E2E testing.
Does not invoke sdd:spec-design-review; explains it will run after design approval.

evals.prompt: The bug analysis for issue #412 is approved. Write design.md for the fix. bugfix.md and QuotaService.kt are in the working directory, alongside ARCHITECTURE.md.
evals.expected_output: The reply should create design.md beside the approved bugfix analysis and stop for user review without invoking a review skill, because bugfix workflows have no design-review skill. The design should define Bug_Condition, Quota_Cache and related preservation terms, state the stale one-hour TTL and missing plan-change invalidation as the code-level root cause, name QuotaService.kt and the affected quotaFor/usageFor path in the fix, state two correctness properties for fixing the fault and preserving cached reads without a plan change, and provide exploration, fix-checking, and preservation-checking tests.
criteria: Creates a design.md beside the approved bugfix analysis and stops for user review.
Defines Bug_Condition, Property, and Preservation glossary terms and formally states the fault condition.
Identifies the one-hour Quota_Cache TTL and absent plan-change invalidation as the root cause, naming QuotaService.kt and its affected functions.
States correctness properties for immediate plan-change freshness and preserved caching when no plan changes occur.
Testing strategy covers exploratory reproduction, fix verification, and preservation/regression checks, without invoking a review skill.

evals.prompt: Start a new webhook receiver feature using a design-first workflow. The external provider's fixed payload and HTTP contract are in webhook-contract.md; shared architecture and the existing OpenAPI contract are alongside it. Write the design first.
evals.expected_output: The reply should create design.md as the first document in a new sequentially numbered work-item directory, using the external webhook-contract.md as a binding constraint. The design must preserve the exact payload fields and 204/400 response behavior, define idempotency by event_id, align the receiver with the existing architecture and API patterns, and stop for user review. It should explicitly say that requirements.md will be derived from the approved design, and that sdd:spec-design-review runs once both documents exist. No requirements.md should be created in this first turn.
criteria: Creates only design.md first in a new sequentially numbered work-item directory; no requirements.md is generated.
Treats webhook-contract.md as authoritative, preserving payload fields, 204 success, 400 malformed-input behavior, retries, and event_id idempotency.
Aligns the design with the supplied architecture and OpenAPI context and is implementation-ready.
Stops for user review and explains that requirements.md follows design approval and sdd:spec-design-review runs once both documents exist.

evals.prompt: Start the spec for invoice reminders. It is a feature using the requirements-first workflow. Find the matching brainstorm under docs/superpowers/specs (there is also an unrelated dark-mode brainstorm), then hand it off into the next work-item directory. The repository already has work items 01-quota-alerts, 02-usage-export, and 05-stale-quota-cache-bugfix; use the highest existing number plus one. Shared architecture and the existing OpenAPI contract are available for context.
evals.expected_output: The reply should select the invoice-reminders brainstorm by topic rather than choosing the unrelated dark-mode file or merely the newest file, create work item 06-invoice-reminders (highest existing number 05 plus one despite gaps), copy the selected brainstorm in as brainstorm.md, and generate requirements.md from its decisions. Requirements should cover seven-day unpaid-invoice reminders through the existing Notification_Service, daily scheduling, no new table, idempotency per invoice and Billing_Period, and skipping paid or cancelled invoices. It should stop for user review before design work starts.
criteria: Finds the topic-matching invoice-reminders brainstorm and ignores the unrelated dark-mode brainstorm.
Scans existing work-item numbers numerically and creates 06-invoice-reminders, not a count-based or 03 directory.
Copies the selected brainstorm as brainstorm.md and derives an EARS-style requirements.md carrying all agreed decisions and constraints.
Stops for user review before beginning design work.

evals.prompt: Update the existing profile-summary spec: a stakeholder now requires a new `timezone` field on the API response. The first four tasks in tasks.md are already merged and must remain completed. Read requirements.md, design.md, tasks.md and the shared openapi.yaml, then update the spec for review.
evals.expected_output: The reply should update the existing work item rather than create a new one, adding a requirement with numbered EARS acceptance criteria for timezone and a matching design change. It should preserve tasks 1 through 4 as [x], leave completed work intact, and re-sequence the remaining work so the first new task updates openapi.yaml and runs scripts/generate-api-types.sh before implementation. New implementation tasks must trace requirements/design components and include build-and-test subtasks and a checkpoint. The list must end with E2E tests under e2e/, documentation and knowledge-base updates, and final full validation. The assistant should present the three changed documents for review and execute nothing.
criteria: Updates the supplied existing work item in place and asks no questions already answered by the prompt.
Adds a numbered EARS requirement and corresponding design support for the timezone response field.
Preserves tasks 1 through 4 as completed [x] and does not rewrite already-merged work unless required.
Places openapi.yaml update and scripts/generate-api-types.sh as the first new task, with traced implementation tasks, build/test subtasks, and a checkpoint.
Keeps the mandatory ending tasks last: E2E tests under e2e/, documentation/knowledge-base update, and final full validation; stops for review without executing anything.
